column1: # iota(4,11) >= 32 ?  the deg(0) = 13 cube under cryptominisat5, over the
# FULL degree-sequence split, one line per sub-cube.  Second opinion for
# cadical's UNSAT at 85123.9 s (docs/ladder/iota4_11.tsv).
# Written by `iota_sym --checkpoint`; a row is appended the moment a
# sub-cube lands, so a reclaimed container loses only what was in flight.
# Resume with the same --checkpoint: UNSAT/SAT rows are skipped, UNKNOWN
# rows are re-run, because UNKNOWN is a budget and not a verdict.
# all_points_used = FALSE, so THE CUBE IS UNSAT ONLY WHEN ALL 1949
# SUB-CUBES ARE UNSAT.  This is NOT the same cover as
# docs/ladder/iota4_11.deg13.tsv, which holds 1939 -- that file was
# written through tools/rung.sh, which passes --ladder and so asks for a
# family on EXACTLY eleven points.  This run was launched from the binary
# without --ladder, so it asks for one on AT MOST eleven points: a
# strictly larger cover, 1939 of it shared and ten more carrying a
# degree-zero point.  UNSAT on all 1949 implies UNSAT on all 1939, so
# this is a sound second opinion and a slightly stronger one; the ten
# extras are redundant, being refuted already by iota(4,10) = 27 < 32.
# Do not merge rows between the two files.  See roadmap 52.1.
# Command:
#   iota_sym 4 11 32 --only-deg 13 --solver cryptominisat5 \
#     --seqprefix 11 --cubecap 2000 --slice 60 --seconds 5400 --threads 4 \
#     --checkpoint docs/ladder/iota4_11.deg13.cryptominisat5.tsv
# THE SECONDS COLUMN IS WALL TIME UNDER CONTENTION and is not comparable
# with the cadical rows in iota4_11.deg13.tsv.  This ran on a 4-core
# session container alongside `cargo test --release` and `make verify`,
# and rows recording 664-820 s against a 600 s solver budget are the
# measure of that, not of the sub-cube.  Same caveat as roadmap 40.2.
# Why the full split and not the prefix-3 split that roadmap 50.3 asked
# for: the prefix-3 split of this cube is 27 sub-cubes, and the four ever
# attempted (under cadical, iota4_11.deg13.p3.tsv) all burned 2400 s
# without landing.  Those four are the first four in lexicographically
# descending enumeration order, covering 553, 325, 180 and 94 full
# sub-cubes -- 1152 of 1939, three fifths of the cube in four pieces.  At
# the 136-491 s a full sub-cube costs, the largest is ~10^5 s of search,
# so a 7200 s budget banks nothing.  The full split is what
# iota4_11.deg13.tsv calls the working granularity.  See roadmap 52.2.
# TWO PASSES, AND THE ROW COUNT IS NOT THE CUBE COUNT.  A 600 s pass ran
# first and banked 3 UNSAT of 20 attempted; an 1800 s pass then resumed
# against this same file, which skipped those 3 and re-ran the 17 UNKNOWN
# ones -- "checkpoint: 3 of 1949 cubes already decided".  The 600 s cap
# was too small for this solver: cryptominisat5 landed 1 of the 8
# sub-cubes it shares with cadical's pass, where cadical landed 5, so
# 600 s here is about a 200 s cadical-equivalent.
# SIX CONTAINER RESTARTS ABSORBED, ZERO ROWS LOST.  The sixth was at
# ~17:53 UTC and killed the driver and all four solvers mid-flight.  On
# restart the same command printed "checkpoint: 129 of 1949 cubes
# already decided" and resumed -- a number that matches an independent
# recount of the distinct UNSAT labels in this file, which is the check
# that makes "zero rows lost" a verified statement and not a hope.
# Every banked UNSAT survived; the only work lost is the partial search
# in the four solvers that were running, which is bounded by the cap.
# **This is the entire argument for the degree-sequence split over the
# whole-cube monolith, and it is now demonstrated six times rather than
# argued once** -- the monolith has twice been killed at ~85000 s and
# lost everything, because a single instance has nothing to check
# point.
# NOTE ON RESTART: phase one re-runs the WHOLE deg(0) = 13 cube for one
# --slice (60 s) before re-splitting.  On a fresh start you will see a
# solver on `sf-sym-11-4-32-c0-...`, with no `seq` in the name, and the
# split only appears a minute later on `...-seq-cNN-...`.  That is not a
# regression to the monolith; it is `plan_phase_two`.  Wait for the
# "checkpoint: N of 1949" line before concluding anything.
# `append_checkpoint` appends unconditionally and never dedups, so a
# re-run leaves the old UNKNOWN row in place beside the new one.  Rows are
# therefore >= cubes attempted, and a label may appear more than once.
# Only UNSAT/SAT rows are load-bearing, and those are written once; to
# count progress, count DISTINCT labels with an UNSAT verdict.
# WHAT THE 1800 s PASS BOUGHT, measured.  Its UNSAT rows land between
# 740.5 s and 1588.7 s -- all above the 600 s cap that had left them
# UNKNOWN, all under 1800 s.  So 600 s was cutting off sub-cubes this
# solver can decide, and the first pass's budget was largely wasted on
# them.  Two sub-cubes are still UNKNOWN at 1800 s, and the largest UNSAT
# used 88% of that budget, so a third pass at a larger cap would likely
# still gain -- it is not yet at the point of diminishing returns.
# STANDING, 21 distinct UNSAT of 42 labels attempted, 0 SAT.
# EVERY SUB-CUBE CADICAL EVER RECORDED FOR THIS CUBE IS NOW DECIDED, AND
# THE TWO SOLVERS AGREE ON ALL OF THEM.  cadical's pass attempted
# fourteen and landed five, leaving nine UNKNOWN at its 600 s cap.
# cryptominisat5 is UNSAT on all fourteen -- the five it confirms, and
# all nine cadical could not decide:
# So the portion of cube 13 that any solver has examined is now fully
# decided and fully agreed.  Seven further sub-cubes are decided beyond
# cadical's fourteen.
# THIS DOES NOT DECIDE THE CUBE.  21 of 1949 is 1%, and iota(4,11) <= 31
# still rests on cadical's whole-cube UNSAT at 85123.9 s.  What it
# removes is the possibility that cadical's nine UNKNOWNs were hiding a
# SAT: they were not, and a SAT among them would have contradicted that
# whole-cube verdict.
#     0   DISAGREEMENTS throughout.  No SAT anywhere, in 68 rows.
# STANDING: 129 UNSAT, 10 UNKNOWN, 0 SAT over 139 labels -- 129 of 1949,
# 228 rows.  **Both windows are now clean sweeps: 8 of 8 and 12 of 12**
# -- the furthest the cap has ever been from its raise condition, and
# the raise stays unarmed.
# (Housekeeping, recorded rather than silently fixed: this block until
# now ended with the sentence "The 8-window is 5 of 8 and the 12-window
# 5 of 12; both say hold and the earlier disagreement is closed."  That
# was stale text from an earlier batch, left in place while the sentence
# above it was updated, and the two flatly contradicted each other.  A
# recount over all 228 rows gives 8 of 8 and 12 of 12.  I have not tried
# to establish which batch the 5-of-8 reading was true for; the point of
# recording it is that a header edited in place accumulates sentences
# that were each true once, and only a recount distinguishes them.)
# **THE RESUME HAS NOW RE-RUN ALL TEN STRAGGLERS AND DECIDED NONE OF
# THEM.**  That is the complete cycle, not a sample of it: every label
# this run carried as UNKNOWN was given a fresh 10800 s and every one
# came back UNKNOWN.  Cost, ten attempts at ~10900 s on four threads,
# about 7.6 wall-hours.  It is the price the resume policy charges after
# each container restart, and it is now measured rather than estimated.
# **THE 8-vs-12 WINDOW TEST IS RESOLVED, AND THE 12-WINDOW WAS RIGHT.**
# This is the one prediction in this file that was written down BEFORE
# its outcome, so it is the only one whose verdict is not a
# rationalisation.
# Recorded at 207 rows, with the two windows disagreeing for the first
# time in the session:
#     last  8 attempts   0 UNSAT / 8    0.00 UNSAT/h   <- raise trigger
#     last 12 attempts   4 UNSAT / 12   0.60 UNSAT/h   <- hold
# The rule says use the 12 and it said HOLD.  Two rows later:
#     last  8 attempts   2 UNSAT / 8    0.38 UNSAT/h   <- no longer zero
#     last 12 attempts   4 UNSAT / 12   0.57 UNSAT/h   <- still hold
# Had the raise fired on the 8-window it would have doubled the cap to
# 21600 s in the batch immediately before the frontier resumed
# converting.  **That is the third time the 8-window would have raised
# wrongly** -- the header previously recorded two, both diagnosed
# afterwards; this one was called in advance.
# WHY THE 8-WINDOW FAILS HERE, WHICH IS A STRUCTURAL REASON AND NOT BAD
# LUCK.  A resume re-runs every UNKNOWN label before advancing, so the
# eight attempts immediately after a restart are guaranteed to be
# straggler repeats -- known-hard instances, selected precisely for
# having failed. They say nothing about the frontier.  Any window short
# enough to sit entirely inside that block will read zero.  The
# twelve-attempt window survives because it is longer than the block of
# stragglers this run has.  **If the straggler count ever exceeds
# twelve, the 12-window inherits the same defect and the rule needs a
# different guard -- most simply, exclude repeat attempts from the
# window and count only first attempts.**  Ten stragglers today; the
# margin is two.
# 4.7% of the cube, and the rung's bound is untouched.  One hundred
# labels attempted was the first round number this pass reached and it
# is worth saying what it bought: 92 sub-cubes decided, 0 SAT, and no
# disagreement with cadical anywhere.  101 now, and the extra label is a
# stall.
# THE RATE HAS FALLEN SIX BATCHES RUNNING AND THE RULE STILL SAYS HOLD.
# UNSAT/h, then 0.52, then 0.70.  It fell six times, sat flat twice, and
# went back UP.  Last batch this header said two flat readings were "the
# first sign the rate may be levelling rather than heading to zero; one
# more flat reading and that becomes the thing to say".  The next
# reading was neither flat nor down.
# **THE RATE IS NOISE AT THIS WINDOW WIDTH AND THIS HEADER SHOULD STOP
# NARRATING ITS SHAPE.**  Three times now a trend has been described
# here and overtaken by the next batch: "monotone decline", "levelling",
# and before them the 0.21 reading that recovered.  Twelve attempts is
# four batches of four, and one batch of three stalls halves it.  The
# raise condition is stated in numbers -- 0 or 1 UNSAT in twelve
# consecutive attempts -- for exactly this reason, and it is the ONLY
# thing that should move the cap.  The sequence above is a record, not a
# trend.  It does NOT trigger a raise, because the
# rule is stated against ZERO and not against the previous reading --
# precisely because this header twice acted on a fall that then
# recovered.  5.11 is ELEVEN UNSAT in the last twelve -- the highest
# this cap has ever read, more than double the 1.74 that opened the
# sequence.  The "decline" is not merely reversed, it is gone, and the
# low reading it was drawn from (0.51) is now the outlier of the series
# by a factor of seven.
# WHAT THE WHOLE SEQUENCE COST AND WHAT IT BOUGHT.  1.74, 1.18, 0.81,
# 3.83.  It fell by a factor of three and rose by a factor of seven,
# and at no point did the numeric raise condition -- 0 or 1 UNSAT in
# twelve -- come close to firing.  Had the cap been raised on any of the
# three shapes this header narrated, the run would have paid 21600 s per
# sub-cube through the cheapest stretch it has had.
# SO THAT THE NEXT SESSION DOES NOT HAVE TO GUESS, the raise condition
# in numbers: **twelve consecutive attempts banking 0 or 1 UNSAT.**  At
# four the cap is still converting; at one it is not, and the argument
# that any nonzero conversion at a larger cap beats 0.00/h applies.  The
# eight-attempt window reads 0.57 and is still not the window to use.
# THE STRAGGLERS: EIGHT LABELS, AND THE SPLIT IS NO LONGER 6-ONLY.
# Four 5-family stallers, in four consecutive batches, every one on a
# first attempt.  The 5-family stands at 19 decided of 23 labels -- a
# 17.4% stall rate against the 6-family's 5 of 30, 16.7%.
# **AND THE STALL-RATE COMPARISON IS NOW WITHDRAWN TOO.**  Three batches
# ago this header read 4 of 19 (21.1%) against 5 of 30 (16.7%), said the
# difference was not significant, and kept "the sign is established" as
# the residue.  Three batches without a new 5-family stall have taken it
# to 4 of 23, 17.4% against 16.7%.  **The sign is gone.**  There is no
# measured difference between the two families on either quantity.  What
# this cost was five batches of narrating a gap that was sampling noise
# in a count of four, and the useful residue is the arithmetic: a rate
# built on FOUR events moves by four points when the denominator moves
# by four, so it could never have separated 17% from 21% at this n.
# **AND THE MEDIAN COMPARISON IS WITHDRAWN, BECAUSE THE MEDIAN HAS NEVER
# BEEN STABLE.**  The 5-family median has taken SEVEN values as the
# family filled in:
# Up, up, up, down, down, up -- and no reading has survived two batches.
# The seventh value is the fifth distinct one, and it is a return to
# 5761, which is the closest this sequence has come to repeating.
# Two batches ago this header said "on both measures the 5-family
# matches the 6-family"; one batch ago it said the 5-family had crossed
# to being worse; at n = 16 the median is 4707 against 6136 and says
# cheaper again.  **The fault is not in the 5-family.  It is in
# comparing families by a median over sixteen points.**  The stall rate
# is a count and survives; the median is withdrawn as a basis for
# comparison until a family is complete.
# THE NINE-PREFIX CANDIDATE WAS PUT UP TO BE TESTED, AND THE TEST CAME
# BACK NEGATIVE.  Last batch this header recorded, explicitly as a
# candidate at n = 3, that both 5-family stallers shared the nine-long
# opening 13,13,13,13,13,12,12,11,11 with a decided sub-cube.  The third
# staller opens 13,13,13,13,13,12,12,11,10 -- a DIFFERENT nine-prefix.
# The candidate is not extended.  Stalls are not confined to one prefix,
# and the pattern is withdrawn rather than restated with the exception
# attached.
# WHAT SURVIVED THE TEST IS BETTER, AND IT IS TWO PREDICTORS AND NOT
# ONE.  Splitting all 99 labels attempted by the length of the leading
# run of degrees >= 12 -- not the run of 13s -- separates DECIDES from
# STALLS far more sharply than leading-13s does:
#     run>=12    decided  stalled   stall rate
#        6         14        1         6.7%   <- NO LONGER ZERO
#        5          5        0         0.0%   <- five labels so far
#        4          1        0         0.0%   <- one label so far
# Recomputed under COUNT of degrees >= 12 as well: **identical, bucket
# for bucket**, so this table is unaffected by the definition change and
# keeps its leading-run form until the two diverge.
# **"ZERO ON BOTH SIDES OF THE PEAK" IS WITHDRAWN, ONE BATCH AFTER THIS
# HEADER SINGLED IT OUT AS THE ONE DESCRIPTION IT HAD NEVER HAD TO
# with run>=12 = 6, so that bucket is 11 decided and 1 stalled, 8.3%.
# The claim died in the batch immediately after it was named the
# survivor, which is itself the lesson: **calling something the survivor
# is a small-sample claim like any other, and this file had eleven
# labels behind that zero.**
# What is left of the description, stated smaller:
#   * The peak at 7 survives -- 30.8% against 8.3% and 2.6% on either
#     side -- and 8 of the 10 stalls are there.
#   * NOTHING with run>=12 of nine or more has stalled, in 35 labels.
#     That half has not moved and is the stronger half.
#   * The bottom of the table is no longer clean.  6 has a stall; 5 has
#     three labels and no stalls, which at n = 3 says nothing.
# On COST AMONG THE DECIDED the two predictors still answer different
# questions -- leading-13s predicts what a decided sub-cube costs (badly,
# and worse every batch), run>=12 predicts whether it decides at all.
# Neither is a model.  Both are descriptions of 114 labels of 1949.
# The same effect is visible inside the 5-family alone, which is where
# it was noticed: by eighth degree, deg8=12 is 12 decided and 0 stalled,
# deg8=11 is 1 decided and 3 stalled.
# COST BY COUNT OF 13s -- NOT by leading run; see the block-sortedness
# note below for why the definition changed.  A READING THIS HEADER IS
# STILL DECLINING TO MAKE:
#    #13s    n     min    median     max
#      8    26     319      2004    2840   <- holds seven of the eight
#      4    21     433      2103    6412   <- OPENING, see below
# The two block-crossing rows moved here from a phantom "lead13 = 3"
# bucket into the 8 bucket, which is where eight 13s structurally
# belong.  That is the table correcting itself, not a new measurement.
# THE DECLINED READING WAS THE RIGHT CALL, AND TWO ROWS KILLED IT.  Last
# batch the 5-family read median 3653 s on eleven points, below both the
# 6- and 7-families, which on its face put a peak at six leading 13s.
# This header refused to claim it on the ground that eleven points is the
# opening of a family and every family opens cheap.  The next two points
# came in at 7412.9 s and 7838.0 s:
#     n = 11   median 3653     "peak at six" looked available
#     n = 12   median 4875     a third of the way to the 6-family
#     n = 13   median 6096     level with the 6-family's 6136
#     n = 14   median 5929     still level; the move was not a blip
#     n = 15   median 5761     and level is where it stayed
# So the apparent peak was an artefact of a family's opening, exactly as
# the refusal said it might be.  This is the second time in this file
# that a reading taken at a family's opening has been overturned by its
# continuation -- the first was the 6-family's own 4806 s at n = 7,
# refuted at n = 25.  The rule that survives both: NEVER READ A MEDIAN
# BEFORE THE FAMILY IS PAST ITS OPENING, and the opening is longer than
# it looks.  n = 13 is still not past it; what is measured is that the
# 5-family is at least as expensive as the 6-family, not that it is
# cheaper.
# AND EVERY FAMILY OPENS CHEAP.  The 5-family's first two sub-cubes cost
# 936 s and 3108 s, against a 6-family median of 6136 s.  Same pattern as
# the 6-family's 731 s opener and the 7-family's 756 s.  A cheap row
# right after an expensive one usually means the enumeration has crossed
# into a new family, not that the frontier has eased -- which is why the
# median per family is the thing to read, and never a single row.
# **THE DEGREE SEQUENCES ARE NOT GLOBALLY SORTED, AND EVERY "LEADING
# RUN" STATISTIC IN THIS HEADER ASSUMED THEY WERE.**  Row 216 is
# [13,13,13,12,13,13,13,13,13,12,0] -- a 12 at position three followed by
# five 13s.  It is the FIRST of 216 rows that is not non-increasing, and
# it is not a bug.  `symbreak` sorts TWO BLOCKS SEPARATELY: point 0 is
# the max-degree anchor, then `deg(1) >= deg(2) >= deg(3)` and
# `deg(4) >= ... >= deg(10)`, because the residual symmetry after fixing
# the anchor member is `Sym({1,2,3}) x Sym({4..10})` and nothing relabels
# across the two.  Re-checked over all 228 rows / 139 distinct labels:
# **0 violate block-wise sortedness, 10 violate global sortedness**, and
# they fall into two families, each walked in order.  The first, now
# complete at seven members:
#      anchor  block1     block2      tail
#   and a SECOND FAMILY, position 8 = 12 instead of 13, now three deep:
# Identical through nine positions; only the last two move, and they
# move as `x + y = 12` with `x` walking down from 12.  The violation is
# exactly "block 1's minimum drops below block 2's maximum", the only
# way a block-sorted pair can fail to be globally sorted.
# **BOTH PREDICTIONS ARE NOW RESOLVED, AND THEY RESOLVED DIFFERENTLY.**
# They were written down before the rows arrived, which is the only
# reason either verdict is worth anything.
# (a) MEMBERSHIP -- CONFIRMED, then immediately widened.  The header
#     said the remaining members were tails `7,5` and `6,6` and then the
#     family ends.  Both arrived, in that order.  It also said "a
#     violator of a DIFFERENT shape would mean the region is wider than
#     this reading" -- and one came in the same batch:
#     than 13.  So the family prediction was exactly right and the
#     surrounding claim was exactly wrong, both inside one batch.  The
#     violators are not one family; that family was the first of
#     several, and the header now expects more shapes rather than more
#     members.
# (b) MONOTONE COST -- **REFUTED.**  The header said: if `6,6` lands
#     above 2840 s the reading survives, if below, the effect is not
#     monotone and that gets recorded rather than explained away.  It
#     landed at **2347.3 s**, below `7,5`'s 2840 and below `8,4`'s 2400:
#     Cost rises steeply from `12,0` to `9,3`, then flattens across
#     `9,3`, `8,4` and `6,6` at 2331-2400, with `7,5` sticking out at
#     2840.  **The minimum-degree reading survives only as far as the
#     first four members.**  Six of the seven sit in a band; calling that
#     monotone was reading a curve through a plateau plus one outlier.
#     Recorded as a refutation because that is what a pre-registered
#     prediction is for.
# **THE SECOND FAMILY, AND WHAT THIS HEADER WILL AND WILL NOT PREDICT
# ABOUT IT.**  The eighth violator opened a new shape and the ninth
# confirmed it is a family too: block 2 is `13,13,13,13,12,x,y` with
# `x + y = 13`, and block-2 sortedness forces `12 >= x >= y`, so the
# complete list is `x = 12,11,10,9,8,7` -- six members, of which `12,1`
# and `11,2` have landed.
#   PREDICTED, and now THREE OF SIX CONFIRMED: tails `10,3` (landed,
#   5658.5), then `9,4`, `8,5`, `7,6`, then this family ends too.  This
#   is the same kind of claim that held exactly for the first family,
#   and it is arithmetic about the encoding rather than a reading of the
#   data -- which is why it is the only part of this section stated as a
#   prediction at all.
#   NOT PREDICTED: anything about their cost -- and the third member is
#   the first real test of that abstention, so it is worth being precise
#   about what it did and did not settle.  The second family now reads
#   2333, 4260, 5659: three points, rising, and rising faster than the
#   first family did over its own first three (319, 1018, 1692).  That
#   is a fact about three numbers.  It is NOT a monotone cost law, and
#   this header still declines to predict the fourth, because the first
#   family ALSO rose monotonically through its first FIVE members
#   three-long rising prefix is weaker evidence than the five-long
#   rising prefix that already failed here once.  **The abstention is
#   not being revised, and the temptation to revise it -- now that the
#   numbers look obliging -- is exactly the thing it was written to
#   resist.**
# Global sortedness held for the first 215 rows only because block 1's
# minimum happened to stay at or above block 2's maximum.  Nothing
# guaranteed that, and this row is where it stopped.
# WHAT IT COSTS, NOW MEASURED BOTH WAYS RATHER THAN ESTIMATED.  Both
# statistics were recomputed under leading-run and under COUNT over all
# 218 rows:
#   * THE STALL TABLE IS IDENTICAL under the two definitions, bucket for
#     bucket.  Both violators keep their >= 12 degrees contiguous at the
#     front, so lead and count agree there.  Nothing in that table moves.
#   * THE COST CORRELATION FOR 13s DOES NOT AGREE, and the difference
#     runs the wrong way for the story this header was telling:
#     Five readings.  Under counts the coefficient sat at -0.21 three
#     times and is now -0.23; the leading-run version has gone -0.14,
#     -0.13, -0.12, -0.10.  **The two series are separating at about
#     0.01 per violator and are now 0.13 apart, from a common value of
#     -0.21 five rows ago.**  That is the rate at which the abandoned
#     definition would have been inventing a decay -- and note the count
#     version moved the OTHER way this batch, so under the right
#     definition there is no decay to see at all.
#     At n = 115, before any violator, the two were the same number,
#     -0.21.  So the apparent further fall to -0.14 this batch is **an
#     artefact of the definition, not a change in the cube.**  Under
#     counts the coefficient is flat at -0.21, which is what the watch
#     item recorded two batches ago and what the leading-run version
#     would have quietly overwritten with a spurious continuation of the
#     decay.
# **THE 13s STATISTIC IS THEREFORE READ AS A COUNT FROM HERE ON.**  The
# >= 12 statistic may keep its leading-run form -- the two agree on every
# row so far -- but it is the same accident and should be migrated the
# moment they diverge.
# This is the ninth item for roadmap 54.3a and a third kind: not a small
# sample, and not a mis-described measurement, but a statistic whose
# DEFINITION depended on an unstated property of its input.
# TWO THINGS MAKE A SUB-CUBE CHEAP, AND THE RANKING BETWEEN THEM HAS
# ALREADY FLIPPED ONCE.  Correlation of UNSAT cost against candidate
# predictors, recomputed over all 91 decided sub-cubes, with the reading
# at n = 67 beside it:
#   The row was labelled "leading 13s" until this batch.  It is renamed
#   because the two readings of that phrase -- the COUNT of 13s anywhere
#   in the sequence, and the LEADING RUN of them -- are now different
#   statistics, and the rename is safe rather than a silent redefinition:
#   checked over all 139 labels, they are **identical on every one of the
#   129 globally sorted ones and differ on all 10 violators**.  A sorted
#   sequence puts every 13 at the front, so count and leading run cannot
#   disagree; they became two statistics exactly when the first violator
#   landed.  Every column left of n = 115 therefore reads the same under
#   either definition, and the table is continuous.  The leading-RUN
#   version, tracked separately above, is at -0.08 and still falling.
# **THE WATCH ITEM FROM LAST BATCH HAS A SECOND READING, AND IT IS STILL
# NOT A FINDING.**  leading-13s has now sat at -0.21, -0.22, -0.21 across
# three measurements, so it has stopped falling for the moment after
# eleven consecutive falls.  Meanwhile run>=12, the statistic this header
# had been calling the steady one, moved -0.33, -0.32, -0.31, -0.28 --
# the largest single step it has taken.  **Nothing is claimed from
# either.**  Three flat readings is the threshold this header set for
# saying leading-13s has bottomed out and it has now reached exactly
# three, which is the moment to be most careful rather than least: the
# threshold was chosen before the data arrived, and a rule met exactly at
# its boundary is the weakest form of confirmation there is.  Wait for
# five.
# **THE "WAIT FOR FIVE" THRESHOLD IS RESOLVED, AND WAITING WAS RIGHT.**
# The fourth reading arrived at n = 129 and it MOVED: -0.23, against
# -0.21, -0.22, -0.21.  So the count never reached five flat readings,
# and had this header called the statistic bottomed out at three -- the
# threshold it had itself set, met exactly at its boundary -- the call
# would have been wrong one batch later.  This is the first pre-declared
# threshold in this file that was met and then deliberately NOT acted on,
# and it is the only one whose continuation vindicated the caution rather
# than punishing it.
